AI Agent Design Patterns

AI agents are becoming increasingly sophisticated, capable of performing complex tasks autonomously.

The most powerful AI systems combine multiple patterns :
- A system might start with planning to structure a complex task
- Use tool use to gather information from external sources
- Apply reflection to evaluate and refine its approach
- Implement ReAct cycles to ground reasoning in real-world feedback
- Leverage multi-agent collaboration when specialized expertise is needed

These design patterns are implemented on top of several core capabilities :
- Memory systems -> For maintaining context and accumulating knowledge
- Language understanding -> For interpreting instructions and information
- Knowledge representation -> For organizing information effectively
- Decision-making frameworks -> For choosing among possible actions

Follow @techNmak for more such insights.

🤖 Do you still think modern #AI is just about #LLMs❓

🎯 To build real, enterprise-grade AI systems ➜ You must master the 5️⃣ pillars of modern AI 👇

1️⃣ Agentic AI
Systems that plan, act, collaborate & learn through feedback. The foundation of autonomous AI.

2️⃣ Generative AI
The creative layer. Text, images, audio & video generated using LLMs, diffusion models & optimization.

3️⃣ Large Language Models (LLMs)
The intelligence core that understands instructions, reasons over context & powers assistants and copilots.

4️⃣ AI Agents
Goal-driven systems combining perception, memory, planning, reasoning & tool use. Digital workers, not chatbots.

5️⃣ Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
The reliability layer. Grounding AI in real, up-to-date data from documents and internal knowledge.

Master these pillars and you won’t just use AI.
You’ll design, deploy & scale systems that solve real problems.

tweets.text:
Without World Models, There Is No AGI. Google Just Proved It.

If AGI ever happens, it will not come from bigger chatbots alone. From the very start of this interview, one thing is crystal clear: without world models, we will never reach AGI. And right now, Google is leading with its world simulator Genie 3.

Here is the core of what Demis Hassabis explains in this conversation:

• World models are the missing core of AGI
Hassabis says his deepest long term focus has always been world models and simulations. Not just language. Not just prediction. Actual internal simulations of reality.

• LLMs are impressive, but incomplete
Language models understand more about the world than expected because human language encodes a lot of reality. Still, language is only a shadow of the real thing.

• What text can never fully teach
Reality includes things text struggles to express:
•3D space and spatial dynamics
•Physical causality and mechanics
•Sensorimotor experience like movement, force, smell, or balance

• Experience beats description
To close the gap, AI must learn from interaction and experience, not just static text. That is how you build an internal world simulator.

• Why Genie 3 matters
With Google DeepMind pushing systems like Genie 3, AI starts to model reality itself, not just talk about it.

• Robots and real world assistants depend on this
True robotics, smart glasses, and universal assistants require AI that understands the physical world you live in, not just your screen.

Bottom line:
AGI will not emerge from better text prediction. It will emerge from systems that can simulate, predict, and understand reality itself. Right now, Google is clearly ahead on that path.

Curious what you think. Are world models the real AGI unlock, or just another stepping stone?
